# libvirt bridge networking — putting VMs on the LAN

By default, libvirt VMs sit on the `virbr0` NAT network and can only
reach the LAN through the host. To make them first-class citizens on
the LAN — directly reachable, with their own IP — replace `virbr0`
with a real Linux bridge over the host's physical NIC.

## References

# https://joshrosso.com/docs/2020/2020-11-13-vm-networks/
# https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6435eNKpyYw

## Inspect libvirt's default DHCP

# Auto-generated; don't edit by hand — use `virsh net-edit default`.
sudo less /var/lib/libvirt/dnsmasq/default.conf

# Sample contents:
#   strict-order
#   user=libvirt-dnsmasq
#   pid-file=/run/libvirt/network/default.pid
#   except-interface=lo
#   bind-dynamic
#   interface=virbr0
#   dhcp-range=192.168.122.2,192.168.122.254,255.255.255.0
#   dhcp-no-override
#   dhcp-authoritative
#   dhcp-lease-max=253
#   dhcp-hostsfile=/var/lib/libvirt/dnsmasq/default.hostsfile
#   addn-hosts=/var/lib/libvirt/dnsmasq/default.addnhosts

## Build a bridge on the fly (non-persistent, for testing)

sudo ip link set enp0s25 down
sudo ip addr del 192.168.1.101/24 dev enp0s25
sudo systemctl status NetworkManager
sudo systemctl status systemd-networkd
sudo systemctl stop systemd-networkd

sudo ip link add name br0 type bridge        # the new "virtual switch"
sudo ip link set enp0s25 master br0          # attach the physical NIC
sudo ip addr add 192.168.4.7/16 dev br0 brd 192.168.255.255

sudo ip link set up enp0s25
sudo ip link set up br0

sudo arping 192.168.1.101                    # ARP probe to verify
sudo route add default gw 192.168.1.1        # default gateway

sudo journalctl -f -u systemd-networkd       # watch for problems

## Persist with systemd-networkd

# /etc/systemd/network/br.netdev — declare the bridge device
[NetDev]
Name=br0
Kind=bridge

# /etc/systemd/network/1-br0-bind.network — bind eno1 to the bridge
[Match]
Name=eno1

[Network]
Bridge=br0

# /etc/systemd/network/2-br0-dhcp.network — give the bridge an IPv4
# lease via DHCP
[Match]
Name=br0

[Network]
DHCP=ipv4
